evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese Character Database, Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: The entry transmits Shuowen’s analysis of 備 as 从人、𤰈聲, and interprets 𤰈 as arrows in a container, also serving as a sound element. It interprets 人 as carrying the arrow container and associates that scene with preparation and completeness. This supports reporting a phonetic analysis alongside the pictorial interpretation; it does not by itself establish the component’s independent historical pronunciation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants (Taiwan)
evidence.text: The entry gives 備’s reading as Mandarin pinyin bèi and quotes Shuowen: 愼也。从人，𤰈聲。 It identifies modern printed 𤰇 as a change from seal-script 𤰈. This is transmitted lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of an ancient sound correspondence.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 備

evidence.source: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》
evidence.text: The entry gives 箙 as fú and defines it as a container for holding arrows, made from bamboo, wood, or leather. CUHK identifies the arrow-container form 𤰈 with 箙 in textual usage. This supports a modern reading comparison between the lexical characters 箙 and 備, but does not establish a historical reading for the depicted object or for component 𤰈.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》— 箙

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese Character Database, Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: The database states that 𤰈 is not included as a headword in that database. It therefore supplies no character-specific historical or modern pronunciation for 𤰈.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 𤰈 lookup

evidence.field: File description／original file link／source and reuse license
evidence.text: The description page identifies 備-bronze.svg as a modern vector drawing in Western Zhou bronze-script style and links the source graphic to Academia Sinica record image 32.F7BC, from 元年師⿸㫃史簋, identified there as late Western Zhou. It states CC0 1.0 reuse. The exact original-file link shown by the inspected page is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3b/%E5%82%99-bronze.svg. This is a redraw, not a photograph of the inscribed artifact; its pixels were not visually inspected in this research stage.
evidence.title: File:備-bronze.svg — Wikimedia Commons

search_audit.query: 備 備 𤰈 說文 从人 𤰈聲 Mandarin pronunciation 𤰈 箙
search_audit.outcome: Opened the CUHK 備 entry and Taiwan Ministry 備 entry; both give the received 从人、𤰈聲 analysis. CUHK’s 𤰈 lookup says that character is not included in its database. Direct Unicode record attempts for 備 and 𤰈 returned internal errors.

search_audit.query: site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=7B99 箙 kMandarin fú; 箙 fú Unihan 備 bèi official dictionary
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Taiwan Ministry dictionary entry for 箙, which gives Mandarin fú and defines the arrow-container object. The codepoint-specific Unihan record was not opened. The Academia Sinica chardb page is evidence only, not a glyph asset; its rights status does not permit using it as an image.

Inspected the exact Commons description page, confirmed its modern redraw description, late-Western-Zhou source attribution and CC0 statement, and opened the listed original-file link to establish the direct image URL.

gaps: No official Unicode codepoint-specific Unihan pages were successfully inspected for 備, 箙, or 𤰈. Do not claim those current readings came from Unihan in this pass.

The local Baxter–Sagart rows from the supplied dossier are not revalidated by the inspected live pages here. No independent 𤰈 reconstruction was found, so a historical component–host sound comparison remains unavailable.

The reading fú applies to the lexical character 箙. It must not be assigned to 𤰈 as a verified character reading solely because CUHK interprets the component as an arrow-container graph used for 箙. Thus, do not populate a sound array that implies 𤰈 = fú without a source explicitly giving that reading.

The proposed whole-graph borrowing of 備 for 箙 is separately reported by CUHK in the dossier. The arrow-container’s original name and pronunciation are not independently recovered here; current Mandarin fú and bèi do not establish the ancient loan relationship.
The direct bronze redraw URL is established from the inspected Commons page, but image pixels were not examined. No visual claims beyond the file description and source attribution are made.

items.period: Late Western Zhou, as identified for the source inscription by the Commons description
items.tradition: Western Zhou bronze-script style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: A modern redraw of 備 in Western Zhou bronze-script style, based on a form attributed to 元年師⿸㫃史簋. The database interpretation describes a person with an arrow container; compare the form cautiously because the pixels have not been visually inspected in this research stage.
items.alt: Vector redraw identified by its source page as 備 in Western Zhou bronze-script style.
items.selection_reason: A provenance-documented bronze-script candidate relevant to the proposed 人 plus 𤰈 analysis; its precise visible features require the harness’s image inspection.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain, as stated on the Commons file description page.

limitations.text: The candidate is documented as a modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph. Its pixel appearance was not visually inspected, so no specific visual feature is claimed here.

The historical pronunciation of 𤰈 was not recovered. The modern Mandarin reading fú belongs to 箙, which sources associate with the arrow-container graph; that association does not establish 𤰈’s own reading or prove a historical sound match with 備.
